sections.heading: Original abstract
paragraphs: Costabel’s 2022 Oberwolfach report asks for a precise description and proof of the observed approximation of nonreal eigenvalues by the discrete dipole approximation away from a real lattice interval. We give an independent proof for bounded particles whose center-selected cubic voxels converge in volume. This includes every bounded Lipschitz particle, with arbitrary grid translations. At each fixed complex frequency, the actual zero-diagonal matrices have no spectral pollution outside the exact static lattice interval; isolated eigenvalues are approximated with algebraic multiplicity and norm-convergent embedded Riesz projections. The proof combines the established static lattice bound of Costabel–Dauge–Nedaiasl with strong static consistency, Hilbert–Schmidt convergence of the sampled dynamic correction and classical spectral approximation. A separate compact, positive-volume, empty-interior support has a nonreal continuum eigenvalue at frequency 10⁻⁴ while every matrix on the grids n⁻¹ℤ³ is 3 × 3 zero. This example clarifies the geometric hypothesis. The classical ingredients and previously announced dynamic work are explicitly credited; first priority is not certified. AI tools were used extensively, and no external human peer review is asserted.

sections.heading: The idea in plain English
paragraphs: The discrete dipole approximation replaces a three-dimensional scattering volume by dipoles on a cubic grid. This paper asks when matrix eigenvalues outside a certain real lattice interval track the continuum volume operator as the grid is refined.

The geometric requirement is that the union of cubes whose centers lie in the particle approaches the particle in volume. Bounded Lipschitz particles satisfy it, even when the grid is translated. The actual matrices keep every diagonal block zero.

At each fixed complex frequency, the result gives stable inverses away from the interval and convergence of isolated eigenvalue clusters with their total algebraic multiplicity. A separate irregular compact support shows why arbitrary point-membership sets cannot be included without a geometric qualification.

sections.heading: The precise result
paragraphs: Let Ω⊂ℝ³ be bounded and measurable, with a chosen representative for deciding center membership. Fix κ∈ℂ throughout the mesh limit. For h>0 choose arbitrary translations a_h, centers x_m=a_h+hm, cells Q_m^h=x_m+h[−1/2,1/2)³ and occupied indices I_h={m∈ℤ³:x_m∈Ω}. Let Ω_h be the union of the occupied cells and assume (G): |Ω_h△Ω|→0.

The matrix is exactly (T_κ^h u)_m=∑_{n∈I_h,n≠m}h³K_κ(x_m−x_n)u_n, with every 3×3 diagonal block zero. Its continuum comparison is S_κ=A_κ−I/3, using the distributional operator and kernel convention in the paper. This shift is part of the statement, rather than a material-contrast conversion.

Let J_lat=cl W(T)=[Λ_−,Λ_+] be the exact closed numerical range of the bounded selfadjoint full static cubic lattice operator. It contains [−1/3,2/3]. Every compact L⊂(ℂ∖J_lat)∩ρ(S_κ) has uniformly bounded discrete inverses for all z∈L and all sufficiently small h. No sequence of matrix eigenvalues can converge to an off-interval point of the continuum resolvent set.

Every continuum spectral point outside J_lat is isolated with finite algebraic multiplicity. For each closed isolating disk whose closure misses J_lat and whose only continuum spectral point is that eigenvalue, the embedded discrete Riesz projections converge in operator norm to the continuum projection. Ranks eventually agree, and enclosed eigenvalues converge with total algebraic multiplicity. Both gap directions for the total generalized spectral subspaces converge, and the matrix norms stay uniformly bounded.

The value-preserving embeddings and continuum projections are extended by zero to the common space L²(ℝ³;ℂ³). The discrete squared norm is h³∑_m|u_m|², making the cell embedding an isometry. An empty occupied set uses the zero-dimensional matrix convention. Bounded sets with boundary of volume zero, including bounded Lipschitz particles, satisfy (G) for arbitrary translations.

Separately, there exists one fixed compact positive-volume support with empty interior for which S_κ has an isolated nonreal eigenvalue at κ=1/10000, while every grid h=1/n, a_h=0 selects only one isolated volume-zero anchor and gives the 3×3 zero matrix. The support is selected at a sufficiently large existential finite index; no effective index or numerical eigenvalue location is claimed.

sections.heading: Why the result holds
paragraphs: Exact finite radial-shell cancellation, a smooth-core near/far split and uniform whole-space tails establish strong consistency of the static cubic lattice operators. Condition (G) gives strong convergence of the membership masks. The static lattice bound itself is established prior work of Costabel, Dauge and Nedaiasl.

For the actual sampled dynamic correction R_κ=K_κ−K_0, the near-diagonal squared-kernel mass is O(δ+h), including the omitted same-cell block. Uniform continuity away from the diagonal and volume control of the changing masks give Hilbert–Schmidt convergence. No integrated-cell replacement or inserted self interaction is used.

Factoring out the selfadjoint static resolvent turns compact multiplication into norm convergence of the compact family. On isolating contours the analytic static term integrates to zero. Strong convergence of adjoint resolvents, obtained at the conjugate spectral parameter, supplies the remaining left-compact product. Norm-close Riesz projections then give equal finite ranks, total algebraic multiplicity and both subspace gaps.

For the obstruction, the intrinsic ball has exactly three constant-field zero modes for S_0, with spectral gap 1/15. An explicit perturbation estimate gives Im tr H_κ≤−2κ³/3+1446κ⁴=−(7831/15000)κ³<0 at κ=1/10000, forcing at least one nonreal eigenvalue. Rational holes in the closed ball yield nested compact empty-interior supports; continuum mask convergence retains a nonreal cluster on one sufficiently large fixed support. Restoring the isolated null anchor makes every rational-grid matrix zero.

sections.heading: Scope and limitations
paragraphs: The affirmative theorem requires the specified center-selected cubic voxels, zero diagonal blocks, a fixed complex frequency and (G). The membership representative matters. The theorem does not classify all irregular compact particles or show that (G) is necessary for every spectral question.

No spectral correctness inside J_lat, convergence rate, mesh-dependent-frequency limit, full operator-norm convergence of the singular static operators or full norm-resolvent convergence is asserted. Individual Jordan block sizes, diagonalizability and individual eigenvector convergence are not promised.
J_lat is the exact closed static lattice interval. Numerically suggested endpoint extrema are not substituted for its definition. Contours and compact resolvent sets must stay outside it.

The irregular support in the separate example fails (G). Its support index and nonreal eigenvalue location remain existential. It neither contradicts the Lipschitz-particle theorem nor proves a necessary geometry condition.

Static lattice bounds, earlier DDA consistency, classical compact spectral approximation, continuum pole theory and sphere perturbation are credited prior work. No new general spectral principle, first DDA consistency analysis or new mechanism for nonreal continuum poles is claimed.

The full announced 2022/2023 time-harmonic DDA manuscript and Rahola’s full article remain outside the bounded source coverage. Their possible overlap and historical priority are unverified; no firstness, exhaustive novelty or worldwide current-open claim is made.

The infinite-dimensional conclusions rest on the analytic proof and credited classical foundations. Finite symbolic, rational and numerical controls are supplementary evidence. This is an unrefereed preprint prepared with extensive AI assistance, without independent human or journal peer review or formal proof-assistant certification.

sections.heading: Original abstract
paragraphs: Let F=ℚ₃ and let E/F be its unramified quadratic extension. We give an explicit checkable argument that the Langlands quotient with segments [4,6],[2,5],[3,3],[1,4],[0,2] is Galois invariant, is not an entire proper parabolic induction, and has no invariant linear form for any Hermitian stabilizer in GL₁₅(E). The analytic proof assembles the period bases and functional equations of Feigon–Lapid–Offen: two invertible nested-segment swaps expose five necessary opposite-lift conditions forming an odd cycle. Noninduction follows from the Lapid–Mínguez ladder-side matching criterion, with all fifteen partition obstructions displayed. The total multiplicity is zero rather than the two predicted by the historical k=1 multiplicity conjecture. Historical priority and overlap with Luo–Zha, DOI 10.1007/s11464-025-0256-0, remain UNKNOWN: their complete paper was unavailable for comparison. No firstness or worldwide novelty claim is made.

sections.heading: The idea in plain English
paragraphs: A representation can carry linear measurements that remain unchanged under a subgroup. This note presents a concrete representation for which every such unitary-group measurement vanishes, even though the representation is unchanged by the field’s Galois symmetry.

The example is specified by five integer intervals. It is the unique irreducible quotient of a standard induced representation. The separate noninduction assertion says that this quotient cannot itself be the entire representation obtained by induction from a proper parabolic subgroup.

The argument uses established period bases and functional equations to force five incompatible binary choices around an odd cycle. An established matching criterion, applied to every partition of the five intervals, excludes all entire proper induced realizations.
The result is an attributed instance of classical representation-theoretic tools. Its exact overlap with Luo–Zha’s earlier announced work remains unknown, and no first-discovery claim is made.

sections.heading: The precise result
paragraphs: Take F=ℚ₃ and its unramified quadratic extension E/F. Work with smooth admissible complex representations. For a≤b, D_K[a,b]=St_(b−a+1)(K)|det|_K^((a+b)/2), using the irreducible-quotient segment convention. Let π be the Langlands quotient of D_E[4,6]×D_E[2,5]×D_E[3,3]×D_E[1,4]×D_E[0,2].

Theorem 1 states that π∈Irr(GL₁₅(E)), π^τ≅π, π is not itself an entire normalized induction from any proper parabolic subgroup, and Hom_(U(V))(π,ℂ)=0 for every nonsingular 15-dimensional Hermitian space V over E/F.

There are two Hermitian isometry classes in this setting. The paper’s total multiplicity is zero rather than two in the historical OWR Conjecture 4 at k=1. The same example is presented as a counterexample to FLO Conjecture 6.12 and the historical unrestricted local unitary converse; established generic and unitarizable positive classes are kept distinct.

sections.heading: Why the result holds
paragraphs: For each fixed Hermitian orbit, the FLO no-earlier-relation hypothesis supplies a complete holomorphic basis of periods on each of three induced orders. Two strict-containment swaps are actual isomorphisms with nonzero diagonal coefficients in these bases.

The correctly oriented reverse-intertwiner functional equation and classical segment L-factors force opposite lift labels at five linked adjacencies. Entire independent open-orbit restrictions justify specialization even when unrestricted periods in a linked-swapped order need not be holomorphic. The resulting odd cycle has no consistent binary labels.

Only containment of proper rank-one images in the quotient kernel is used. No general equality generating that kernel is assumed. Langlands classification and the additive constituent property reduce any entire induced realization to a partition of the five segment occurrences. Each partition has a ladder side and an explicit directed matching obstruction under the Lapid–Mínguez criterion.

sections.heading: Scope and limitations
paragraphs: The stated example uses the specific characteristic-zero p-adic field F=ℚ₃, its unramified quadratic extension, and smooth complex coefficients. It is not an assertion for all fields or coefficient categories.

Unitary periods refer to stabilizers of Hermitian forms. They do not assume π is unitarizable. Unramified character-line data do not assert that π is spherical. The quotient remains a quotient of parabolic induction; only an entire proper induction is excluded.

The written proof uses deep classical FLO, JPSS and Lapid–Mínguez results as explicitly cited dependencies. Finite scalar and graph diagnostics do not compute Hom spaces or prove those source theorems.

Complete periods for a fixed Hermitian orbit, normalized versus unnormalized operators, the extra quadratic-character twist, and the same-parameter ring involution are essential conventions. No separate kernel-generation disproof is claimed.

Historical priority and all substantive overlap with Luo–Zha, DOI 10.1007/s11464-025-0256-0, remain UNKNOWN. Their publisher abstract and dated workshop announcement establish a prior kernel-generation counterexample claim, but not the exact segments, proof mechanism or period consequences. The present construction may overlap, be contained in, or be superseded by that work.

No exhaustive literature absence, independent first discovery or current worldwide-open assertion is made. This is an unrefereed preprint prepared with extensive AI assistance, without external human or journal peer review or formal proof-assistant certification.
